correctness.rationale: The theorem uses labelled configurations, strict synchronous out-neighbor majority with eleven neighbors, and counts temporal orbits before taking affine classes. I independently built the entire successor array by vectorized bit counts. Its fourth-return locus has 2 fixed points and 14,168 nonfixed states, none fixed by the second iterate. Every input first hits that locus by step 10; exactly 1,012 first hit at step 10 and they all hit a consensus. This rules out every other recurrent period and proves both sharp identity statements. All entry-time counts and basin totals match. Canonicalizing by the minimum phase and then applying all 253 affine permutations reproduces the fourteen stated classes, free action on temporal orbits, and individual basin counts. The pointwise complement identity holds on the entire periodic four-state locus, so complementation preserves each temporal orbit, hence every affine class. The four final-shell representatives, sizes and complement pairings also match. This is exhaustive for the specified graph, not an all-prime argument.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration, not formal verification or an extrapolation to other orders.

value.rationale: Independently of the duplicated census, the affine classification has mathematical use: it determines stabilizers and the complete per-family basin sizes for a canonical symmetric directed system, rather than only the distribution of eventual periods. Half-complementarity identifies complementation with a temporal half-turn on every nontrivial attractor, while the depth-ten initial shell exhibits complement pairing of distinct spatial classes. These are meaningful refinements that the aggregate table cannot supply.
residual_risks: Value here is a finite symmetry-resolved classification, not a general theorem about Paley tournaments.
